prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1411; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is not named on the policy and does not live with the policyholder.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a left-turn collision at an intersection. The claimant reports being struck by an oncoming vehicle while turning, and reports a shoulder injury from the impact.

Entry 2: Reviewed the scene photos and the statement from the other driver, who describes the same sequence of events. Damage to both vehicles is consistent with the reported impact and direction of travel.

Entry 3: Two independent witnesses and the responding officer confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the crash. No prior damage to the vehicle is on record, and nothing indicates the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: The claimant's account has stayed the same across every call and interview so far. The shoulder injury fits the type and force of the collision, and the claimant mentioned an old minor strain in the same area that fully healed years ago.

Entry 5: Medical treatment has run a bit longer than is typical for this kind of shoulder injury. Reviewing the treatment notes to understand the recovery timeline before making any determination.

Entry 6: The driver is not listed on the policy and does not live with the policyholder, which is noted in the file for coverage review. The claimant is not represented by an attorney, and all correspondence has gone directly to the claimant.
